mechanism_narrative: The consistent four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -66.4% to -57.6%, indicates an ongoing recovery in non-essential activity that will continue to drive further increases over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility from -51.4% to -37.3% at t-0w signals a surge in outdoor activity and public comfort, which will directly translate into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility does not increase over the next two weeks despite PARKS mobility rising by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The observed inverse relationship where RESIDENTIAL mobility consistently decreases while RETAIL_REC increases signifies a fundamental shift in daily routines away from home, directly boosting retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or RETAIL_REC mobility decreases over the next four weeks, or the inverse correlation breaks down.

mechanism_narrative: The parallel and consistent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility over the last four weeks indicate a gradual return to office-based work and commuting patterns, which will incrementally boost weekday retail activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT mobility reverses its upward trend, or RETAIL_REC mobility stagnates despite continued increases in these proxies.

mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reflecting essential out-of-home trips, demonstrates growing public confidence in shared spaces, which will quickly spill over into non-essential retail and recreation within the next week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines or RETAIL_REC mobility does not show an increase in the immediate next week.

mechanism_narrative: A combined signal of RESIDENTIAL mobility falling by over 1 percentage point and PARKS mobility rising by over 10 percentage points week-on-week indicates a strong public preference for out-of-home and outdoor activities, directly boosting retail and recreation within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week AND PARKS mobility rises by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility does not increase within two weeks, despite the specified concurrent changes in RESIDENTIAL and PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery observed across RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, PARKS, and the decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a systemic return to pre-pandemic activity levels, which will sustain and accelerate the upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: A majority of the specified mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, PARKS, RESIDENTIAL) reverse their positive or negative (for RESIDENTIAL) trend over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent increase in WORKPLACES mobility, maintaining levels above -50% from baseline, suggests an underlying policy or corporate drive for return-to-office, which will gradually increase weekday foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation areas over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -50% from baseline
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility falls below -50% from baseline, or RETAIL_REC mobility does not show a corresponding increase over the next four weeks.
